name: foodbank-client
description: Food bank management client: referrals, sessions, pick lists and stock.

scripts.dry-run: CLOUDFLARE_ENV=production npm run build && wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir .wrangler/dry-run
scripts.deploy: CLOUDFLARE_ENV=production npm run build && wrangler deploy
scripts.check: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run api:types:check && npm run cf-typegen && npm run dry-run && npm test

//overrides: Two stale peer ranges, both overridden rather than downgrading to match them.
eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y 6.10.2 is the latest release and still caps its eslint
peer at 9. It works under eslint 10 — there is a test asserting it still
catches a real violation, so this is verified rather than assumed. Overriding
keeps us on the same eslint major as the server.
openapi-typescript 7.13.0 caps its typescript peer at 5.x, but it is only ever
run as a CLI that writes a .d.ts — it does not typecheck our source. Confirmed
generating the real spec under typescript 6.
Revisit both when upstream widens its range.
brace-expansion is a security fix, not a peer range. GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg is a
DoS (unbounded expansion, OOM) patched only in 5.0.8 — the 1.x and 2.x lines
are end-of-life at 1.1.17 and 2.1.3 and were never backported. Two dev-only
tools drag them in transitively: eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y via minimatch 3, and
openapi-typescript via @redocly/openapi-core and minimatch 5. npm's suggested
fix is to downgrade both packages by a major, which for jsx-a11y means 6.4.1 —
predating flat config, so it would break eslint entirely. Forcing the patched
brace-expansion instead keeps both tools current. brace-expansion exports one
function and minimatch only calls that, so the major jump is safe here; the
test suite and a real lint run are what confirm it.
